messages:
anne: Quick proposal: introduce an elastic lanes feature for Dedicated reserved pools. Lightweight burst affordance that gives short, predictable overage capacity with preemption and clear billing rules. Wanted quick reactions on launch criteria and autoscale interactions. :thinking:

anne: High-level idea: each reserved pool can opt-in to one or two elastic lanes (fast and slow). Lanes allow short bursts beyond the committed capacity (for example up to 3x) for a short window (30 to 120s). Bursts consume burst tokens that are either prepaid (carryover credits) or billed as overage. When capacity is tight, lane allocations are preemptable and degrade to a fallback model variant or lower QoS queue.

anne: Questions for the group: what safety signals do we need to launch (SLOs, max eviction rate, cost delta)? What should autoscale do while a lane is active? How do we surface this in the Console and SLA docs?

dave: Implementation note: easiest path is to treat lanes as soft reservations backed by a low-priority ephemeral fleet. Autoscaler options: a) spin up ephemeral nodes when bursts exceed commit, or b) reuse existing headroom. Option a is cleaner for isolation.

dave: Pilot suggestion: use option a with ephemeral nodes and a cooldown of 5 minutes to reduce churn. We can add opportunistic reuse later if customers prioritize cost. :+1:

maria: Safety signals we need: p99 and p99.9 latency for burst requests, percentage of bursts that get preempted, and customer visible error rate. Block launch if user-facing evictions during bursts exceed 0.5 percent for pilot customers. Also need controls to avoid noisy neighbour amplification. :eyes:

kevin: Contract note: language must state lanes are best-effort, preemptable, and billed separately as burst credits or overage. Decide whether bursts count toward Dedicated commit calculations; my vote is separate. Customers will need predictable pricing and an opt-out path.

sophie: Console ideas: per-pool burst budget meter, historical burst usage graph, post-burst breakdown (tokens used, cost, preemptions). UI toggle for lane enable and lane policy (max multiplier, window length, preemption priority). Tooltip copy: lanes are best-effort and may be preempted to preserve committed capacity.

dave: Config sketch for pilot:
```
{
  pool_id: pool-1234,
  elastic_lanes: [
    { name: fast, max_multiplier: 3, window_secs: 60, token_mode: prepaid, preemption_priority: 100 }
  ]
}
```

maria: Preemption policy: recommend token-based aging plus fairness. Each burst alloc consumes a token with TTL. Under pressure eviction order sorts by (preemption_priority, token_age, tenant_priority_score). This gives deterministic behavior and lets us report eviction exposure in the SLA.

anne: Autoscaler interaction: during bursts the autoscaler should not immediately scale the committed pool by default. Pilot default: spin up ephemeral nodes from a separate fleet labeled burst-only. If bursts persist beyond a configured threshold (for example 10 minutes), flag for ops and suggest committing additional capacity.

kevin: Billing modes to support: prepaid credits with monthly carryover, pay-as-you-go burst overage, and a small included allowance. Map these to sales SKUs.

sophie: For testing, provide a sandbox mode: bursts allowed but billed to test credits and visible in Console as test usage. Helps customers validate without billing surprises.

dave: Dev checklist for pilot: feature flag, ephemeral fleet and scaling hooks, preemption comparator, telemetry events (burst.start, burst.end, preempt.evicted, cost.charge). Canary with three pools: small, mid, enterprise.

anne: Proposed launch criteria (pilot to beta):
- Pilot run for four weeks with three customers
- Less than 0.5 percent user-facing evictions during bursts
- Measurable cost delta per pool under 10 percent for typical burst patterns
- Telemetry visible in Console and billing export enabled
- Contract language and opt-out UI live

maria: Also require a postmortem runbook and an automatic alert when preemption rate exceeds 0.2 percent per hour for any pilot pool.

kevin: Sales needs a one-page summary of tradeoffs and pricing bands. I will draft after billing modes are finalized.

anne: Suggested timeline: two sprints for runtime and autoscale hooks, one sprint for Console, billing, and docs, then pilot. Owners: dave (eng) runtime, sophie (DX) console, kevin (sales) contract, maria (SRE) safety gating.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature-flag scaffolding to canary org tomorrow 18:00 UTC. :rocket:

anne: Thanks all. Action items: dave to post PR link and ETA, sophie to prototype UI mockups, kevin to prepare draft contract text, maria to write alerting playbook. Reconvene in one week. :+1:

kevin: sounds good.

maria: posted alerting playbook draft to docs repo, will share link here when ready.
